title: Review policy document
description: A plain-English, human-authored policy document for one playbook. This is the ONE home for all prescriptive human input into a review: general rules, scoped guidance, and 'regardless of what the corpus shows, treat our position as X' statements. It is deliberately NOT derived from the corpus -- the OPF playbook's evidence/digest carries what the corpus HAS shown (descriptive precedent), while this document carries what a human says we DO (prescriptive policy). The playbook feedback loop corrects derivation errors of fact and never edits this file. Filename convention: <playbook_id>-policy-v<N>.json, where N is the integer `version` below.

$schema.description: Optional local schema pointer for editor tooling.

playbook_id.description: The playbook this policy governs, as registered in playbooks/registry.json. Generic: nothing in the schema or the consuming code is specific to any one playbook_id.

version.description: Monotonic integer version. Editing the policy bumps this by 1 and re-stamps `approval`, then the bundle is re-bound. Deliberately an integer, not semver: a policy edit is a governance event, not a semantic-compatibility event.

title.description: Human-readable title, shown in the Rules admin page.

description.description: What this policy covers and any caveats a reviewer/approver should know.

approval.description: Governance stamp. A policy is only prescriptive input a human has signed off on, so who approved which version, when, is recorded here.

status.description: `draft` until a human with authority approves this exact content. Never stamp `approved` on content an approver has not actually reviewed.

approved_by.description: Name and role of the approver, e.g. 'Jane Doe, Head of Legal'. Null while draft.

approved_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of approval. Null while draft.

supersedes.description: The `version` this one replaces, or null for the first version.

note.description: Free-text context for the approver: what changed, what needs scrutiny.

harvested_from.description: Provenance when this policy's content was migrated out of an earlier artifact, so an approver can diff intent against the source they previously approved. content_hash MUST be recomputed from the actual harvested revision and is always verified directly against `path` on disk. git_blob_sha/git_commit are recorded IN PAIR and are OPTIONAL: they additionally anchor content_hash to a git revision when the harvested source was already a landed commit at harvest time. They MUST be omitted -- never fabricated -- when no such landed commit exists yet (e.g. the source was edited in the same changeset that records the harvest); a commit object reachable from no pushed ref resolves on the machine that made it and nowhere else. The source may later be deleted, and a fresh-history public cut carries no history to recover it from, so this record is what makes the policy stand alone.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the RAW BYTES of the harvested revision of `path`.

git_blob_sha.description: Optional. The git blob object whose bytes hash to content_hash; recorded only when git_commit is also recorded.

git_commit.description: Optional. A commit already in history whose tree resolves `path` to git_blob_sha; recorded only when git_blob_sha is also recorded.

carried_determinations.description: Determinations of record made by an approver on the HARVESTED SOURCE that this policy carries forward. The point of a policy document is that such decisions live in one versioned, signed home; harvesting the rules without them would strand the decision. Carrying a determination does NOT approve this document -- `status` governs that.

source_legal_approval.description: The approval block recorded on the source artifact, reproduced here for the approver's benefit. It signs the SOURCE's exact content, not this document.

determinations.description: Each determination and the policy rule(s) that now carry it.

flagged_for_approver.description: Questions the harvest deliberately did NOT decide because they are legal judgment calls. An approver must resolve each before `status` moves to `approved`.

rules.description: The prescriptive rules. Order is presentation order; it carries no precedence meaning.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within this document. Cited verbatim by the attribution manifest as a change's authorizing input, so it must not be recycled across meanings.

strength.description: `must`: binding when applicable. If a must rule appears inapplicable or in tension with the clause at hand, the reviewer FLAGS for attorney review -- never silently overrides in either direction. Every must rule is also re-read against the finished redline by the closing model self-check. `should`: weighs heavily, but the model may decide against it on the facts and say why.

topic.description: Optional grouping label for display in the Rules admin page (e.g. 'indemnification'). Advisory only: scope that actually constrains a rule belongs in its `text`, because `text` is what the model reads.

text.description: The rule in plain English, exactly as a human wrote it. Rendered verbatim to the model and to the Rules admin page -- never paraphrased, summarized, or templated by code.
